deep.reconstruction:
Context (pp. 41-43). Grothendieck studies a system Σ of n pseudo-lines in the projective plane, possibly with multiple points. To each pseudo-line D he attaches a combinatorial/topological polygon Δ_D of order 2(n-1): the cyclic sequence of crossings of D with the other lines, read on the double cover, i.e. the sphere. He also uses 'specialization' and 'generization' operations: pull an auxiliary line L across the crossings until it merges with D, or the reverse. These give 'generization arcs' on Δ_D and transition isomorphisms ω(Δ_L) → ω(Δ_D). The aim is to glue all the Δ_D along these arcs into one cell complex. The previous page ends on an obstruction: the generization arcs attached to the vertices of a fixed D overlap each other ('empiètent les uns sur les autres').

This page proposes the remedy. Read 'Pour pallier cet inconvénient, on peut songer à multiplier chaque D de Σ en autant d'exemplaires qu'il y a de sommets.'
(1) Replace each D by copies indexed by the vertices s on D. The basic objects become 'contact elements', i.e. incidence pairs (flags) (D,s) with s a vertex on D.
(2) For each contact element there are then exactly two 'exceptional' generization arcs, on Δ_D or the relevant copy, and these no longer overlap.
(3) If s is a simple vertex (two lines through it), the two exceptional arcs bound a topological bigon.
(4) If s is a multiple point, the two exceptional arcs together with the two 'ordinary' generization arcs at s bound a convex topological polygon, the 'polygone local'. In modern terms this is the 2k-gon dual to a k-fold crossing.
(5) Gluing these bigons and local polygons onto the previous pieces 'completes a compact surface'.
(6) The oriented graph used before (the specialization/flip graph) is to be modified. Each exceptional vertex is replaced by the set of diagonals of its local polygon. This is a resolution/blow-up of multiple points into local polygons.

The next page formalizes the outcome as the 'Déploiement' X(Σ) of the system. It is a compact surface with two cellular subcomplexes K and L. K is 4-valent and has exceptional and ordinary edges; the exceptional edges form a union of circles. L has vertices of even order. A counting rule holds: every face of K carries 2n points of L, counted with reduced multiplicity.

So the page is the step that turns the family of polygons Δ_D into a closed surface with a 4-valent cell structure (a map in the sense of dessins). It does this by passing from lines to flags and inserting a bigon or local polygon at each contact element.
errors: No clear mathematical error, but the claims are asserted without proof. These include: exactly two exceptional arcs per contact element; the arcs bound a bigon at a simple vertex and a convex polygon at a multiple vertex; the gluing gives a compact surface (closed, no boundary, a manifold rather than a pseudo-manifold). These are verified only implicitly, by the axioms on the next page.
It is left unclear how the copies of D indexed by different vertices are glued to each other. Whether the ordinary arcs at s belong to a single copy is also unclear.

The phrase about the oriented graph is a sketch, with a crossed-out false start ('Mais il faudrait détermi...'). The rule replacing an exceptional vertex by the set of diagonals of the local polygon is not justified.

ideas.what: Replacing pseudo-lines by contact elements / flags (D,s) and duplicating D once per vertex, to separate overlapping generization arcs
ideas.modern_name: Passage to the flag (incidence) complex; blow-up/separation along vertices
ideas.usually_credited_to: Standard technique (flag complexes, barycentric subdivision); not specifically attributed in pseudoline literature

ideas.what: Local polygon at a multiple point: the exceptional and ordinary generization arcs bound a 2k-gon (a bigon if the point is simple)
ideas.modern_name: Dual 2k-gon tile of a k-fold crossing in a zonotopal/rhombic tiling; local sequence/allowable sequence at a multiple point

ideas.what: Gluing the polygons Δ_D plus bigons/local polygons into a compact surface, the 'déploiement' of a pseudo-line system, carrying a 4-valent complex K and a complex L with a 2n-points-per-face rule
ideas.modern_name: No exact modern counterpart; closest are cell complexes of pseudoline arrangements, flip graphs/higher Bruhat orders B(n,2), and maps/dessins on surfaces
ideas.where_published: Possibly alluded to among the combinatorial-topology themes of the Esquisse d'un programme (1984); unsure

ideas.what: Modifying the oriented specialization graph by replacing each exceptional vertex with the diagonals of its local polygon
ideas.modern_name: Resolution of degenerate (non-simple) arrangements into simple ones; flips across polygonal 2-cells
ideas.usually_credited_to: Ringel; Felsner–Weil (sweeps); higher Bruhat order literature

missed.claim: Grothendieck sketches a canonical compact surface (the 'déploiement') attached to any pseudo-line system, including non-simple ones. It is built from one polygon per line (indexed by flags) plus bigons and local polygons, and the construction is left as a sketch. As far as I know no such surface invariant of pseudoline arrangements has been studied in the literature.
missed.quote: On a fait ce qu'il fallait pour compléter une surface compacte, en recollant à les précédents des bigônes ou convexes.
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: It would give a surface or map (dessin-like) invariant of oriented-matroid rank-3 data. Its genus and Euler characteristic could be computed from flag counts. This could be compared with flip-graph cell complexes and higher Bruhat orders.

missed.claim: The local polygon at a multiple point is the dual zonotopal tile, and the diagonals replacing exceptional vertices recall flips/resolutions. Together these implicitly link Grothendieck's specialization/generization formalism to later zonotopal tiling and higher Bruhat order theory.
missed.quote: remplaçant chaque sommet "exceptionnel" par l'ensemble des diagonales du polygone local
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Grothendieck's specialization/generization formalism, with transition isomorphisms ω, may be a stack-like or descent-style framework for the poset of arrangements. That viewpoint is absent from the combinatorial literature.

deep.surprise_reason: This is an intermediate technical fix within an unpublished and little-known project on pseudo-line systems. The ingredients (flags, local 2k-gons, gluing) are routine. The overall 'déploiement' surface seems not to be in the literature, but this page alone only patches an overlap problem.
transcription_corrections: 'Pour Montpellier [?] : est inconvénient [?] ou peut-être [?]' should read 'Pour pallier cet inconvénient, on peut songer à'.
'qui ne comptent [?] pas' should read 'qui n'empiètent pas'.
'Sinon, en eux [?]' should probably read 'Sinon, ces arcs'.
'il n'y a pas de raison de [?] rentrer [?] — qui est un tricorne [?] !' is probably 'il n'y a pas de raison d'insister — qui vivra verra !' (uncertain).
'convexe sur Δ_D' is plausible but the word is unclear in the image ('couvert'?).
The insertion above 'Mais il faudrait...' looks like 'Elle se ramène à graphe' or similar, not 'Le graphe dual du graphe'.
'précédent, par celui déduit en' is likely 'précédent, par celui déduit du précédent en'.
